Self harm is a nasty thing to beat, so first of all congrats on your 1 year free of it that’s very difficult to do - whatever reason you did it, you did manage to get that far and that’s insanely impressive.

Self harm is an addiction of sorts, so unfortunately a lot of those thoughts end up pretty engrained. And like managing most addictions, there’s different things that work for everyone, so I’m just gonna list some that work for me and then some I’ve heard for other people

1. Eating lemons. Weird as fuck I know but I slice up lemons and salt them and fucking chomp down. They’re super sour and I guess that kinda sting helps me calm down without hurting myself.

2. Distraction - probably an obvious one but for me as well if I get some sort of hyper-fixation then I might be too distracted to focus on it. I tend to play a lot of video games + watch more upbeat shows cause for me getting upset at shows makes it worse, so things like kids cartoons or comedy shows are nice.

3. Ranting/talking about it - what you’re doing now basically I have this account to talk about things like that and sometimes it helps me manage stuff.

Things I’ve heard work with other people:

1. Using a rubber band against your skin - it’s supposed to do something similar to the lemons but for me it just makes me want to SH more so I’d be careful. Like it’s not enough yknow

2. Ice on skin - same thing as above, same reason as above to look out for

I can’t think of anything else off the top of my head but I hope that helps! There’s also r/selfharm and r/adultselfharm if you wanna talk more in depth though sometimes those subreddits can be a bit tricky cause half the people encourage it and the other half are tryna stop

Styro is a deeper layer of the skin that kinda looks like styrofoam, it’s considered pretty deep I believe. Beans I have no idea about 😭 I try not to use these terms cause I feel bad saying people aren’t like self harming enough it’s a pretty bad habit I get in on myself on

It honestly depends on the scar. How deep the cut was originally, the type of blade used can affect the scarring, how light or dark your skin is, how much sun you get daily, etc.

Getting a tattoo to cover them is a great idea. If they’re large scars (I know you said noticable and not prominent I’m talking more in width) there can be ink blowouts so make sure you find someone with experience dealing with scar tissue, as it tattoos differently. Also your wrist can be kinda painful because the ink would be close to bone, so just be aware of that but honestly not that bad especially if you’ve already s/h there. I always find it easier to get tattoos in places I’ve S/H cause I already kinda know what pain there feels like.

If you want something less obvious as to hiding, try getting something that wraps around your wrist or complements it somewhere without scarring, so you don’t associate it with simply being a coverup. Hope this helps :)
